Not in accordance with the law.
A person born to unmarried parents.

ex.ja: まず彼は未婚の母から生まれた私生児である。

A banned or unlawful item.

ex.ja: 彼の無能ぶりに誰もが苛立ち始めた。

Temporary inability to sleep.

ex.ja: 彼は不眠症にかかりやすい。

ex.ja: 不眠症はとても一般的です。

note.ja: ラテン語 in（否定）+ somnus（眠り）。「不眠症」。somnambulist（夢遊病者）と同じ somn。

ex.ja: 彼女は一人息子の死をいたみ悲しんだ。

ex.ja: 私たちは皆事故による死者に哀悼の意を表した。

ex.ja: 彼の死は皆を悲しませた。

note.ja: 古英語 murnan（嘆く）から。「嘆く・悼む」。mourning と同じ。

Pertaining to the Universe, cosmos or physical reality, as opposed to the spiritual world.
An unremarkable, ordinary human being.

Any substance capable of stopping or slowing a specific chemical reaction.

A penetration by hackers, a computer virus, etc.

intrusion.ety: From Middle English intrusioun, from Old French intrusion, from Medieval Latin intrūsiō, from intrūdō, from Latin in- + trūdō.

ex.en: Sorry for the intrusion.
ex.ja: お邪魔してしまってすみません。

note.ja: intrude（侵入する）+ -sion。in + trudere（押す）。「押し入ること」→「侵入」。thrust と同系。

Reverse, opposite in order.
An inverted state: a state in which something has been turned (properly) upside down or (loosely) inside out or backwards.
The reverse of any procedure or process.
To compute the bearing and distance between two points.

inverse.ety: Recorded since 1440, from Latin inversus, the past participle of invertere (“to invert”), itself from in- (“against, in”) + vertere (“to turn”).

note.ja: in（反対に）+ vers（向ける）+ e。向きを反対にした →「逆の・反対の」。

en: Having the order or direction exchanged; for example, turned upside down, reversed, or in any other way opposite or contrary and swapped.
Having the lowest note transposed an octave higher.

ex.en: Through the lens the image was inverted.
ex.ja: レンズを通ると像は逆になった。

ex.en: Place your skis in an inverted V.
ex.ja: あなたのスキーを逆Ｖ字型にしなさい。

note.ja: invert（逆にする）+ -ed。in + vertere（回す）。「逆さの」。inverted commas（引用符）。

en: The act of irritating or annoying.
The state of being irritated.

irritation.ety: Borrowed from Middle French irritation, from Latin irrītātiō, from irrītāre (“to excite”). By surface analysis, irritate + -ion.

ex.en: There was no irritation on his part.
ex.ja: 彼としては少しもいらいらしてなかった。

ex.en: Her mood graduated to irritation.
ex.ja: 彼女の気分は次第にいら立ちはじめた。

note.ja: irritate（いらだたせる）+ -ion。ラテン語 irritare（刺激する）。「いらだち・炎症」。

en: Any word used as the key to a code.
Any word used in a reference work to link to other words or other information.
To tag with keywords, as for example to facilitate searching.

note.ja: key（鍵・重要な）+ word（語）。「キーワード」。

en: Expending or bestowing profusely; profuse; prodigal.
Superabundant; excessive.
To give out extremely generously; to squander.
To give out to (somebody) extremely generously.

lavish.ety: From Middle English laves, lavas, lavage (“extravagant, wasteful, prodigal”), from lavas (“excessive abundance”), from Old French lavasse, lavache (“torrent of rain”); possibly later conflated in some senses by Middle English laven (“to pour out”), equivalent to lave + -ish. ex.ja: 彼は金を惜しみなく使う。

ex.en: He's lavish with his money.
ex.ja: 彼は金を惜しみなく使う。

ex.en: The real estate broker was lavish in his spending in Ginza.
ex.ja: その不動産屋は銀座で気前よく金を使った。

note.ja: 古フランス語 lavasse（どしゃ降り）から。laver（洗う）。「惜しみない・ぜいたくな」。

en: A means of providing the necessities of life for oneself (for example, a job or income).

livelihood.ety: From Middle English liflode, from Old English līflād (“course of life, conduct”), from līf (“life”) + lād (“course, journey”), later altered under the influence of lively, -hood. Compare life, lode.

ex.en: Life and livelihood are the same thing.
ex.ja: 金と命は同義語だよ。

ex.en: How is livelihood in America these day?
ex.ja: 最近のアメリカ人の暮らし振りはどうですか。

ex.en: The ordinary people had their livelihood in farming rice.
ex.ja: 庶民のなりわいは、米をつくることだった。

note.ja: 古英語 līflād（人生の道）から。life + lode（道）。のちに likelihood の影響を受けた。「生計」。

en: Consisting of a variety of ingredients or parts.
Having diverse characteristics, abilities or appearances.

miscellaneous.ety: Borrowed from Latin miscellāneus, from miscellus (“mixed”), from misceō (“mix”).

ex.en: I keep all my miscellaneous files in this folder.
ex.ja: このフォルダーに、「その他」に分類される全てのファイルを入れて保管しています。

ex.en: That drawer is full of miscellaneous items.
ex.ja: あの引き出しの中は雑多なもので溢れかえっている。

note.ja: ラテン語 miscellaneus（混ぜた）から。miscere（混ぜる）。「種々雑多な」。mix と同じ。

An assembling or review of troops, as for parade, verification of numbers, inspection, exercise, or introduction into service.
To be gathered together for parade, inspection, exercise, or the like (especially of a military force); to come together as parts of a fo…
To collect, call or assemble together, such as troops or a group for inspection, orders, display etc.

muster.ety: From Middle English musteren, borrowed from Anglo-Norman mostrer, Middle French monstrer, moustrer (whence the noun monstre, which gave the English noun), from Latin mōnstrō (“to show”), from moneō (“to admonish”). Cognate with French montrer (“to show”), Italian mostrare (“to show”), Spanish mostrar (“to show”). See also monster.

ex.en: I mustered up my courage and went there.
ex.ja: 私は思い切ってそこに行った。

ex.en: I'm sure it'll work out, so muster your courage!
ex.ja: きっとうまく行くから、勇気を出せ！

ex.en: She finally mustered up the courage to ask him for more money.
ex.ja: 彼女はついに勇気を出して彼の借金の申し込みをした。

note.ja: ラテン語 monstrare（示す）から。「（兵を）集めて見せる」→「召集する・奮い起こす」。demonstrate と同じ。

en: A string or flat strip of pasta or other dough, usually cooked (at least initially) by boiling, and served in soup or in a dry form mixed…
An object which is long and thin like a noodle (sense 1).
To hum or sing (a tune) at a low pitch or volume.

noodle.ety:
Borrowed from Dutch noedel (“noodle”), or from its etymon German Nudel (“piece of pasta, noodle”); further etymology uncertain, probably a variant of Knödel (“dumpling”), from Middle High German knödel (“dumpling; small knot”), and then either:
* from knode, knote (“knot”) (from Old High German knodo, knoto (“knot”), perhaps ultimately related to Proto-West Germanic *knappō (“knob; boy”)) + -el (diminutive suffix); or
* from Ladin menùdli (“small dough dumpling in soup”), probably from Latin minutulus (“very small, tiny”) (in the sense of food chopped into small pieces), a diminutive of minūtu

ex.en: You're right. The noodle broth here is a bit expensive.
ex.ja: その通りさ。ここの麺の出汁はちょっと値が張るんだ。

note.ja: ドイツ語 Nudel から。「麺」→（俗）「頭」。

en: Originally, the DuPont company trade name for polyamide, a copolymer whose molecules consist of alternating diamine and dicarboxylic acid…
A stocking originally fabricated from nylon; also used generically for any long, sheer stocking worn on a woman's legs.

nylon.ety: Coined by the company DuPont in 1938. According to the company, the name was formed from the random generic syllable nyl- + the common fiber suffix -on (as in rayon and Dacron), said to be ultimately from cotton.

ex.en: These nylon socks wash well.
ex.ja: このナイロンソックスは、洗濯がきく。

ex.en: Nylon stockings often run.
ex.ja: ナイロンストッキングはすぐ伝線する。

note.ja: 1938年にデュポン社が作った合成繊維の名。語源ははっきりしない。

en: To ride across or beyond something.
To ride over the top of something, usually forcibly.
A mechanism, device or procedure used to counteract an automatic control.
A royalty.

override.ety: From Middle English overriden, from Old English oferrīdan, equivalent to over- + ride. Cognate with Dutch overrijden, German überreiten, Danish override.

ex.en: The President vetoed the bill, but Congress overrode his veto.
ex.ja: 大統領はその法案に対して拒否権を行使しましたが、議会が再度それを無効にしました。

ex.en: Under the Constitution, the lower chamber's resolutions override those of the upper chamber.
ex.ja: 憲法の規定に従い衆院の議決が参院に優越する。

note.ja: over（上を）+ ride（乗る）。「上を乗り越える」→「覆す・優先する」。

en: An allotrope of oxygen (symbol O₃) having three atoms in the molecule instead of the usual two; it is a toxic gas, generated from oxygen …
Fresh air, especially that breathed at the seaside and smelling of seaweed.
To treat with ozone.

ozone.ety:
From German Ozon, coined 1840 by Christian Friedrich Schönbein, from Ancient Greek ὄζον (ózon), neuter participle of ὄζω (ózō, “I smell”), in reference to its pungent odour.
The “fresh air” sense is from an erroneous former belief that seaweed contains and releases ozone.

ex.en: Without the ozone layer, we would be in danger.
ex.ja: もしオゾン層がなければ、私たちは危機に直面しているだろう。

ex.en: The ozone layer continues to be further destroyed every year.
ex.ja: オゾン層は年々破壊が進んでいる。

ex.en: This chart illustrates the function of ozone layer.
ex.ja: この図はオゾン層の機能を説明している。

note.ja: ギリシャ語 ozein（におう）から。独特のにおいから「オゾン」。

en: Extreme, irrational distrust of others.

paranoia.ety:
Learned borrowing from Ancient Greek παράνοια (paránoia, “madness”), from παράνοος (paránoos, “demented”), from παρά (pará, “beyond, beside”) + νόος (nóos, “mind, spirit”).
By surface analysis, para- (“abnormal, beyond”) + nous (“mind”) + -ia (“(medical) condition”).

en: The hard durable surface placed directly atop the ground, as on a street or sidewalk.
Interior pavement, as in a cathedral.
Pertaining to the material used for pavement, or to the surface itself.

note.ja: pave（舗装する）+ -ing。ラテン語 pavire（突き固める）。pavement と同じ。

To harass with importunity; to pursue with persistent solicitations; to annoy.

ex.ja: 彼は人々を宗教により迫害しました。

ex.en: Some early religion's leaders were persecuted by their enemies.
ex.ja: 初期の宗教指導者の中には敵対する人々に迫害されたものもいる。

ex.en: The Romans persecuted Christians.
ex.ja: ローマ人はキリスト教徒を迫害した。

note.ja: per（どこまでも）+ secu（追う）+ te。しつこく追い回す →「迫害する」。prosecute（起訴する）と混同注意。

The holding of multiple benefices.

Ancient; very old, outdated, etc.

ex.ja: なんで英語の代名詞"I"はいつも大文字表記なのかわからない。

ex.ja: 関係代名詞は「接続詞+代名詞」のはたらきをしています。

ex.ja: 中学生が英語を学ぶ際の最難関の一つが関係代名詞です。

The human mind as the central force in thought, emotion, and behavior of an individual.

ex.ja: 彼はレースにのぞんで精神統一した。

In a disc brake, the metal disc attached to the wheel hub.

A lonely or deserted place.

solitude.ety: From Middle English solitude, from Old French solitude, from Latin sōlitūdō. By surface analysis, sole + -itude.

ex.ja: 彼は毎日好んで独りで過ごす時間を持つ。

A place of domination by, or refuge or survival of, a particular group or idea.

ex.en: Many conspiracy theorists leverage unverifiable statements and claim them as facts.
ex.ja: 多くの陰謀論者が、未検証な発言を利用してそれらを事実と主張する。

en: in that; in that place; in him/her/it.

therein.ety: From Middle English theryn, ther-inne, þer-in, from Old English þǣrin, þǣrinne, from Proto-West Germanic *þārin, *þārinna, from Proto-Germanic *þarin, *þarinna, equivalent to there + in. Cognate with Saterland Frisian deerin (“therein”), West Frisian dêryn (“therein”), Dutch daarin (“therein”), German Low German daarin (“therein”), German darin, drin (“therein”), Danish deri (“therein”), Swedish däri (“therein”), Icelandic þar í (“therein”).

ex.en: Therein lies the problem.
ex.ja: そこに問題がある。

note.ja: there + in。「そこに」。法律文で使う硬い言い方。

en: Shaped like a triangle.
Of, or pertaining to, triangles.

triangular.ety: From Middle English triangulare, trianguler, triangulere, from Old French triangulaire, triangulier and Latin triangulāris. By surface analysis, tri- + -angular.

en: Honest, and always telling the truth.
Accurately depicting what is real.

truthful.ety: From truth + -ful. Piecewise doublet of trothful, from Middle English trouþeful.

ex.en: She brought up her children to be truthful.
ex.ja: 彼女は子供を正直であるように育てた。

ex.en: I don't think he is truthful.
ex.ja: 彼の言うことは本当ではないと思う。

ex.en: His report was truthful.
ex.ja: 彼の報告は真実だった。

note.ja: truth（真実）+ -ful。「正直な」。

en: Being everywhere at once: omnipresent.
Appearing to be everywhere at once; being or seeming to be in more than one location at the same time.

ubiquitous.ety: From ubiquity + -ous, from Medieval Latin ubīquitās, from Latin ubīque (“everywhere”), from ubī̆ (“where”) + -que (“each, ever”). Compare ubiety.

note.ja: ラテン語 ubique（どこにでも）から。ubi（どこに）。「どこにでもある」。

ex.ja: 彼のふしだらな行為は気付かれずにはすまなかった。

ex.en: In a town you may pass unnoticed, whereas in a village it's impossible.
ex.ja: 都会では気付かれず通り過ぎることもあるだろうが、村の中ではそうはいかない。

The spiritual beliefs of the Ewe/Fon of West Africa, practiced chiefly in Benin and in the south of Togo.
To bewitch someone or something using voodoo

ex.en: I don't believe in voodoo.
ex.ja: ブードゥー教は信じていません。

en: The practice of witches; magic, sorcery, or the use of supernatural powers to influence or predict events.
Black magic; the use of witchcraft for evil means.

witchcraft.ety: From Middle English wicchecraft, wicchecreft, from Old English wiċċecræft, equivalent to witch + -craft.

ex.en: This is not witchcraft.
ex.ja: これは魔法ではありません。

note.ja: witch（魔女）+ craft（技）。「魔術」。

en: Sexual intercourse by a married person with someone other than their spouse. See more synonyms at Thesaurus:cuckoldry
Lewdness or unchastity of thought as well as act, as forbidden by the sixth/seventh commandment; sinful sexual behavior as a category.

adultery.ety: With change of suffix, from the Old French adultere (“violation of conjugal faith”) (in Bernard of Clairvaux, Sermons, 12c.), a learnèd borrowing from Latin adulterium, from adulterō. Replaced the older form avoutrie, from the inherited Old French forms avouterie or aoulterie, while keeping its suffix. Compare French adultère (“adultery”). Displaced Old English ǣwbryċe. Not related to adult.

ex.en: According to many religions, adultery is a crime.
ex.ja: 多くの宗教において、姦淫は罪悪とされる。

ex.en: The crime of adultery was abolished in 1947.
ex.ja: 昭和２２年に姦通罪は廃止されました。

note.ja: ラテン語 adulterare（混ぜ物をする・汚す）から。adulterate（混ぜ物をする）と同じ。「不倫」。adult とは別語源。

en: Having the faculty of quick motion in the limbs; apt or ready to move; loose-jointed.
Characterised by quick motion.
Agile software development.

agile.ety: From earlier agil, borrowed from Latin agilis (“agile, nimble”), from agō (“do, act; move”). See agent.

ex.en: This athlete is strong and agile.
ex.ja: このアスリートは、力もあるし機敏だ。

note.ja: ag（動かす・行う）+ ile。すばやく動ける →「機敏な・身軽な」。

ex.en: He anonymously donated a large sum of money to the Red Cross.
ex.ja: 彼は匿名で赤十字に多額のお金を寄付した。

en: Severity of manners or life; extreme rigor or strictness; harsh discipline.
Freedom from adornment; plainness; severe simplicity.

austerity.ety: From Ancient Greek αὐστηρότης (austērótēs, “bitter, harsh”). Morphologically austere + -ity.

ex.en: He practices austerities almost like a monk.
ex.ja: 彼は僧侶に近い禁欲生活をしている。

ex.en: The fiscal austerity may lead to an overkill of the economy.
ex.ja: 緊縮財政政策は経済を冷やし過ぎることになるかもしれない。

ex.en: Fiscal austerity is considered to be an answer to the rampant inflation.
ex.ja: 激しいインフレに対処するには、緊縮財政が必要だと考えられている。

note.ja: austere（厳しい）+ -ity。ギリシャ語 austēros（渋い・厳しい）。「緊縮・簡素」。

ex.ja: あなたの新車はずいぶん高そうですね。

ex.en: I'm awfully sorry that I was late.
ex.ja: 遅れまして、誠に申し訳ありません。

ex.en: We are awfully fed up with his long speech.
ex.ja: 私たちは彼の長話に全くあきあきしている。

note.ja: awful（ひどい）+ -ly。「ひどく」→（口語）「とても」。

ex.ja: 彼が花束をプレゼントしてくれたの。

ex.en: Tom gave a bouquet of flowers to Mary.
